name: Casino / Slots
concept_focus: Building a complete program: files, functions, modules, tests, simulation, classes, saves and a README

story.title: The Silver Reels
story.client: Auditor Pell of the Gaming Guild
story.hook: Ekse Ouens P Diddy has bought the Silver Reels and swears every machine is fair. Pell has been sent to prove otherwise, and needs someone who can build a slot machine from an empty file, grow it into a real project, test it, measure it a million spins deep, and hand over a README anyone can follow.

acts.title: Act I: The Machine
acts.goal: One file, one machine: create casino.py, run it, read its errors, and build a round that pays honestly.

acts.title: Act II: The Session
acts.goal: Functions, a main() and your first modules: the machine becomes a program you can read.

acts.title: Act III: The Audit
acts.goal: Weighted reels, a million spins, tests that prove the maths, and the bugs the numbers expose.

acts.title: Act IV: The House
acts.goal: A Machine class, saved bankrolls, a menu, a README anyone can follow, and a machine that is yours.

boss_lore: Ekse Ouens P Diddy bought the Silver Reels with cash and confidence. Every reel is re-weighted, every jackpot sign is lit, and his hype men shout about wins nobody ever sees. He swears the house is fair. Pell wants proof.
boss_brief: Bring the finished Silver Reels project: casino.py with a menu, a Machine class in its own module, weighted reels, a payout table checked best first, validated bets, a session summary, simulate() and theoretical_rtp() that agree, tests that pass, saves that survive a broken file, and a README that gets a stranger playing.
boss_twist: Diddy brings his own machine and swears it returns 97%. Write audit(machine, spins=100000, seed=None) that returns the measured return, the hit frequency and the largest drawdown of a 100-coin bankroll; compute the machine's theoretical return from its weights; and make Machine refuse (raise ValueError) any table whose theoretical return is above 100%. Print both returns for his machine and for yours.

twist_2.label: Phase 2: Diddy opens the roulette table
twist_2.quest: Diddy moves you to his roulette table on the same bankroll. Build roulette in its own module, roulette.py, with red/black, odd/even and single-number bets, a Bet class that knows its own payout, and the zero that gives the house its edge. Add it to the menu, and add tests for every bet type's payout.

twist_3.label: Phase 3: The audit report
twist_3.quest: Pell needs a report Diddy cannot argue with. Add a report command that audits every machine and the roulette table and writes audit_report.md: each game's theoretical and measured return, hit rate and drawdown in a table. Explain in the README how to produce the report, and keep every test passing.

mobs.name: The Coin Rat
mobs.concept: Project folders, files and running Python
mobs.encounter: Make the silver_reels project folder with casino.py inside, run it from the terminal and see your bankroll printed.
mobs.contract: Pell's first rule: a machine that does not run does not exist. Make the file, run it, and show the Rat your purse.

objectives.label: Make it run
objectives.brief: Every real project lives in its own folder. Make a folder called silver_reels in your workspace and create casino.py inside it (+ New file, then silver_reels/casino.py). Store a starting bankroll of 100 coins in a variable and print a welcome line that shows it. Run it from the Forge terminal: cd silver_reels, then python casino.py.

objectives.label: Explain the run
objectives.brief: Explain what happens when you type python casino.py inside silver_reels: which file runs, why the folder you are in matters, and in what order its lines execute.

objectives.label: Predict the purse
objectives.brief: Predict what prints if you subtract a bet of 15 from the bankroll before the welcome line, then check it.

mobs.name: The Spin Imp
mobs.encounter: Spin three reels from a list of symbols and show the line.
mobs.contract: Three reels, chosen fresh each spin. The Imp wants proof you know how many lines are possible.

objectives.label: Spin three reels
objectives.brief: Keep the symbols in a list and pick one at random for each of three reels, then print the line like | CHERRY | BELL | SEVEN |.

objectives.label: Unstick the reels
objectives.brief:
A rival machine spins like this:
```python
line = [random.choice(symbols)] * 3
```
Explain in a comment why it always shows three of a kind, and make sure your three reels spin independently.

objectives.label: Count the lines
objectives.brief: Predict how many different lines three reels of five symbols can make, then compute it in code.

mobs.name: The Payout Mimic
mobs.concept: Dictionaries and checking conditions in order
mobs.encounter: Pay each winning line from a payout table, best win first.
mobs.contract: The Mimic pays a jackpot like a cherry. Build a payout table and check it from the most valuable win down.

objectives.label: Build the table
objectives.brief: Store the payouts in a dictionary (for example three sevens, three bells, any two cherries) and write payout_for(line, bet) that returns the winnings.

objectives.label: Best win first
objectives.brief: Check combinations from most to least valuable so three sevens never pays as a smaller win, and show one line of each kind paying correctly.

objectives.label: Explain the order
objectives.brief: Explain what goes wrong if you check any two cherries before three cherries.

mobs.name: The Broken Bet
mobs.encounter: Fix a bet prompt that crashes on words and accepts impossible bets.
mobs.contract: Someone wrote the bet prompt in a hurry. It crashes when you type ten, and it lets you bet coins you do not have.

objectives.label: Fix the prompt
objectives.brief:
This is the rival machine's bet prompt. Put it in casino.py, run it and type ten:
```python
bet = int(input('Bet: '))
bankroll = bankroll - bet
```
Fix it so words and numbers below 1 ask again instead of crashing, and a bet bigger than the bankroll is refused.

objectives.label: Read the traceback
objectives.brief: When int('ten') crashes, which line does the traceback point at, and what is ValueError: invalid literal for int() telling you?

objectives.label: Survive bad bets
objectives.brief: Show your prompt handling a word, 0 and more than the bankroll in a row, then accepting a good bet.

mobs.name: The Debt Ghoul
mobs.concept: One honest round, start to finish
mobs.encounter: Join bet, spin, pay and bankroll into one round that repeats until you quit or go broke.
mobs.contract: The Ghoul feeds on bankrolls that go below zero. Put the whole round together and starve it.

objectives.label: Play one round
objectives.brief: Write one full round: ask for a bet, spin, pay from your table, update the bankroll and print what happened.

objectives.label: Keep playing
objectives.brief: Repeat rounds until the player types quit or the bankroll cannot cover the smallest bet.

objectives.label: Starve the Ghoul
objectives.brief: Prove the bankroll can never go below zero: find the path where it could, fix it, and show a session that ends exactly at 0.

objectives.label: Keep the evidence
objectives.brief: Run a five-round session from the terminal and paste its output as a comment at the bottom of casino.py.

mobs.name: The House Edge
mobs.encounter: Turn the spin into a function that returns its line.
mobs.contract: Pell cannot audit logic smeared across a file. Start with one clean function.

objectives.label: Write spin()
objectives.brief: Write spin(symbols) that returns a list of three symbols, and use it in your round instead of the inline code.

objectives.label: Predict the return
objectives.brief: Predict what print(spin(['A'])) shows, and what print(spin) shows without the brackets.

objectives.label: Return, not print
objectives.brief: Explain the difference between a function that prints its line and one that returns it, and why your payout code needs the return.

mobs.name: The Croupier
mobs.concept: Organising a program: functions, docstrings and main()
mobs.encounter: Give casino.py a shape: small functions, docstrings and a main() behind the __name__ guard.
mobs.contract: The Croupier only deals at a tidy table. No loose code at the bottom of the file.

objectives.label: Small functions
objectives.brief: Split casino.py into small functions (ask_bet, spin, payout_for, play_round), each with a one-line docstring saying what it returns.

objectives.label: Add main()
objectives.brief: Put the session in main() and call it under if __name__ == "__main__": so importing casino.py never starts a game.

objectives.label: Explain the guard
objectives.brief: Explain what if __name__ == "__main__": does when you run casino.py, and when another file imports it.

mobs.name: The Tally Ghost
mobs.encounter: Track the session's spins, wins and money, then summarise it.
mobs.contract: The Ghost keeps the books nobody else wants to keep. Every spin, every win, and the truth at the end of the night.

objectives.label: Keep the books
objectives.brief: Track spins, wins, the biggest win, total bet and total won in one dictionary, and print a clear summary with net change and win rate when the session ends.

objectives.label: Check the maths
objectives.brief: Predict the summary for a short scripted session (fix the random seed), then check it.

mobs.name: The File Splitter
mobs.encounter: Move the reels and the payout table into their own files and import them.
mobs.contract: One file is fine for one machine. Pell is auditing a whole floor. Split the machine so each file has one job.

objectives.label: Make reels.py
objectives.brief: Create reels.py holding the symbol list and spin(). Nothing else.

objectives.label: Make payouts.py
objectives.brief: Create payouts.py holding the payout table and payout_for().

objectives.label: Import them
objectives.brief: Import both modules in casino.py, delete the old copies, and show python casino.py still plays a full session.

objectives.label: The name trap
objectives.brief: Explain why naming one of your own files random.py would break import random everywhere in this project.

mobs.name: The Greed Spirit
mobs.encounter: Add a loss limit and a play-again loop, and remove the duplicated code your session grew.
mobs.contract: Greed never stops on its own. Give the player limits, and give the code a clean-up.

objectives.label: Set a loss limit
objectives.brief: Let the player set a loss limit at the start and end the session the moment it is reached.

objectives.label: Play again
objectives.brief: When a session ends, offer a new one with a fresh bankroll without restarting the program.

objectives.label: Say it once
objectives.brief: Find code you have written twice (printing the line, checking the bet) and replace each pair with one function used in both places.

objectives.label: Count true
objectives.brief: The summary says 11 spins after 10. Make sure your spin counter counts each spin exactly once and starts at the right value.

mobs.name: The Weighted Reel
mobs.encounter: Make some symbols rarer than others with weights.
mobs.contract: Real machines are not fair dice. Every symbol has a weight, and the weights are the secret.

objectives.label: Weigh the reels
objectives.brief: Give every symbol a weight and spin with random.choices(symbols, weights) so sevens are rare and cherries common.

objectives.label: Predict the counts
objectives.brief: With weights 1, 3 and 6 for three symbols, predict roughly how often each appears in 1,000 spins.

objectives.label: Weights and payouts
objectives.brief: Explain why the payout table has to change when the weights change.

mobs.name: The Million Spins
mobs.encounter: Simulate many spins and measure the real return to player.
mobs.contract: Pell does not trust a machine until it has spun a million times without a human pressing a button.

objectives.label: Simulate
objectives.brief: Write simulate(spins, seed=None) that plays automated spins at a fixed bet and returns the total bet, the total won and the return to player (won divided by bet).

objectives.label: Hit frequency
objectives.brief: Also return the hit frequency: the share of spins that paid anything.

objectives.label: Seeds
objectives.brief: Predict what happens if you run simulate(1000, seed=7) twice, and then twice without a seed.

mobs.name: The Test Witch
mobs.encounter: Write tests that prove the payouts and the bankroll rules.
mobs.contract: The Witch believes nothing she has not tested. Neither should you.

objectives.label: Test the payouts
objectives.brief: Create test_casino.py with test functions that assert payout_for pays every row of your table correctly and pays 0 for a losing line.

objectives.label: Test the bankroll
objectives.brief: Add tests that a bet bigger than the bankroll is refused and the bankroll never goes below zero.

objectives.label: Read a failure
objectives.brief: Run your tests from the terminal and break one on purpose. What does a failing assert print, and how do you find which test failed?

mobs.name: The Rigged Reel
mobs.encounter: Find the bug that makes a rigged simulation report an impossible return.
mobs.contract: A rival auditor's simulation says a rigged machine returns thousands of percent. Find out why before Diddy quotes it.

objectives.label: Fix the audit
objectives.brief:
This is the rival's simulation:
```python
def rtp(spins):
    bet, won = 0, 0
    for _ in range(spins):
        bet = 1
        won += payout_for(spin(SYMBOLS), 1)
    return won / bet
```
Find the bug, make sure your own simulate() does not share it, and explain the fix in a comment.

objectives.label: Catch it next time
objectives.brief: Write a test that would have caught this bug: simulate a machine whose return you can work out by hand and assert the result matches.

objectives.label: Why it lied
objectives.brief: Explain in one or two sentences why the bug inflated the result.

mobs.name: The Balancer
mobs.encounter: Work out the theoretical return from the weights and tune the table to a target.
mobs.contract: Pell wants a machine that returns 95% in theory and in practice. Prove both.

objectives.label: Exact return
objectives.brief: Write theoretical_rtp() that computes the exact expected return from the reel weights and the payout table, without spinning.

objectives.label: Tune the table
objectives.brief: Adjust the payout table until the theoretical return is between 94% and 96%.

objectives.label: Theory meets practice
objectives.brief: Add a test that simulate(200_000, seed=1) lands within 1% of theoretical_rtp().

objectives.label: Same return, more risk
objectives.brief: Two machines both return 95%. Explain how one can still feel much riskier to play.

mobs.name: The Machine Smith
mobs.encounter: Turn the machine into a Machine class you can make many of.
mobs.contract: Diddy's floor has forty machines. Nobody copies the code forty times.

objectives.label: Build the class
objectives.brief: Write a Machine class holding its reels, weights and payout table, with spin() and payout_for() methods.

objectives.label: Two machines
objectives.brief: Create two machines with different symbols and tables that share one player bankroll, and play a round on each.

objectives.label: Explain self
objectives.brief: Explain what self refers to when you call machine_a.spin(), and why machine_b is not affected.

mobs.name: The Ledger
mobs.encounter: Save the bankroll and lifetime stats, and load them next time.
mobs.contract: The house remembers every coin. So should you.

objectives.label: Save and load
objectives.brief: Save the bankroll and lifetime stats to casino_save.json next to casino.py when the program ends, and load them when it starts. Build the path from Path(__file__).parent so it works whichever folder you run from.

objectives.label: Survive a broken save
objectives.brief: If casino_save.json is missing or broken, start fresh with a clear message instead of crashing. Test it by deleting a bracket from the file.

objectives.label: Predict the file
objectives.brief: Predict what casino_save.json contains after a session that ends on 87 coins after 12 spins, then open it and check.

mobs.name: The Memory Thief
mobs.encounter: Rebuild your payout checker from memory in a blank file.
mobs.contract: The Thief stole your notes. Prove the knowledge was yours, not the file's.

objectives.label: Rebuild it
objectives.brief: Close payouts.py and casino.py. In a new file memory_check.py, rebuild payout_for and its table from memory, checking the most valuable wins first.

objectives.label: Prove it
objectives.brief: Under it, write asserts for a top win, a small win and a loss, and run the file until they pass.

objectives.label: Compare
objectives.brief: Compare your rebuild with the original: what did you remember, and what did you do differently?

mobs.name: The Front Door
mobs.concept: A finished program: a menu and a README
mobs.encounter: Give the casino a menu and a README anyone can follow.
mobs.contract: Pell's report goes to people who have never seen your code. They need a front door and instructions.

objectives.label: Open the front door
objectives.brief: Add a main menu: play slots, choose a machine, run an audit (a simulation), show lifetime stats, or quit. A bad choice asks again.

objectives.label: Write the README
objectives.brief: Write README.md in silver_reels: what the project is, how to run it (cd silver_reels, then python casino.py), how to run the tests, and one line on what each file does.

objectives.label: Follow it yourself
objectives.brief: Follow your README step by step from a fresh terminal and add a Known issues section with anything that tripped you up.

objectives.label: Play-test it
objectives.brief: Have someone else (or a scripted run) play five rounds, note two things that confused them in README.md, and fix one of them in the code.

mobs.name: The Showman
mobs.encounter: Design a machine that is yours: a theme, symbols and a bonus round.
mobs.contract: Diddy only books acts nobody has seen before. Build a machine that is unmistakably yours.

objectives.label: Your machine
objectives.brief: Create your own themed Machine (your symbols, weights and payout table) and add it to the menu.

objectives.label: Your bonus round
objectives.brief: Design and build a bonus round triggered by a special line (free spins, pick-a-box, a multiplier wheel...) with its own rules.

objectives.label: Defend the design
objectives.brief: Explain one design decision you made for your machine and whether it is fair to the player.
